findings.title: Task 2's success criterion is false: tests that build `LanguageSnapshot` directly cannot pass unchanged after the enum addition
findings.description: Task 2's Success is "the full `tests/metrology/` suite passes unchanged", but adding four `SnapshotMetric` members makes `LanguageSnapshot._one_measurement_per_metric` (snapshot_models.py:193) reject any snapshot built with only the four 400 metrics. Verified two 400 tests do exactly that: `test_snapshot_models.py:225` (`test_json_round_trip_is_lossless`) constructs a `LanguageSnapshot` with `measurements` for only `file_length`, `function_length`, `lint_count` and `type_errors` (lines 229–244), and `test_render.py:61` builds `python_snapshot()` with the same four measurements — the latter also fails the summary test because the new metric lines have no handling yet. The second bullet of Task 2 only repairs `PythonAdapter.metrics`, which covers `test_take.py` (it iterates `set(SnapshotMetric)` via real adapters) but not these directly-constructed fixtures. The fix is small — enumerate `SnapshotMetric` or append the new metrics as `no_adapter`/absent in those two builders — but the task says nothing will change, so a junior executor will hit unexpected failures and either misdiagnose them or edit tests without any task authorizing it. Task 2 should explicitly list which 400 tests need the new members added (and note this is test-fixture maintenance, not a change to the SC-12 "edited only for the rename" rule, which covers length tests only). The Task 30 checkpoint "Every Success Criterion maps to a passing test" won't catch this either, since the claim lives in Task 2's success line rather than an SC.

findings.title: Render tests that assert new-metric line shapes belong to Task 27 but Task 2 breaks them first
findings.description: Task 27 tests "each new line's shape matches the API Contracts example", but `test_render.py`'s fixture (`python_snapshot`, line 36) becomes structurally invalid at Task 2 for the reason above, and its expected line set won't contain the four new metrics until Task 27. The task pair works if Task 2 repairs the fixture's measurement list; if the above finding is addressed, this resolves with it. No action beyond the Task 2 edit.

findings.title: Success-criteria coverage is complete
findings.description: Every SC in the slice design has a task with an explicit SC citation: fixture values (SC3) in Tasks 4/6, duplication boundaries (SC4) in Task 11/15, the token ceiling with a `monkeypatch` trigger (SC10) in Task 11, freshness and `report_stale` detail (SC5) in Task 21/22, real-report fixtures (Technical Requirements) in Task 18/20, failure-mode rows (Technical Requirements) asserted signal-and-outcome in Tasks 9/11/20/21/24, and the contract freeze (Integration) checked by diff in Task 30 with the coverage-wiring check in Task 25. Task 30's final checklist makes the mapping explicit, which is the right backstop. No missing-item finding.

findings.title: Sequencing and test-with pattern are correct
findings.description: Tasks 3→4, 5→6 (module then tests), 7→8 (carry then emit), 10→11, 12→13, 14→15, 16→17, 19→20, 21→22, 23→24 each place tests immediately after implementation. `MeasuredFunction` (7) precedes `complexity.py` (8), the read-and-decode helper (7) precedes `measure_duplication`'s use of it (10), fixtures (18) precede the reader (19), and the reader (19) precedes `read_coverage` (21). No circular dependencies. Task 25 (adapter coverage wiring) has no committed sibling test of its own, but Task 26 follows immediately as its snapshot-level test, which is the correct pattern.

findings.title: Proportionality is appropriate for the slice size
findings.description: 30 tasks with efforts mostly 1–3 (one 4) matches a slice adding four metrics across two languages with no new dependencies; nothing is inflated with implementation detail the design doesn't require, and no task is so large it should split — Task 10 (Effort 4) is the heaviest but its seven sub-bullets are the whole of D3 and are individually checkable. No task file split is proposed; a single file is right for this size.
